cand.title: 48th Annual Canadian Business Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony & Celebration
cand.excerpt: High evidence specificity and dated organized hospitality activity; accessibility is discounted where the venue is already committed.
cand.ledgerVenue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, Lower Level

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two current named relationship-entry contacts: Oli Maynard-Langedijk, Director, Business Development & Partnerships, and Erin Barton, Chief Development Officer, both in JA Canada’s current national directory. Oli’s professional profile explicitly includes CBHF sponsorship; Erin oversees the team containing the CBHF/events manager in the October 2026 role description. They are relevant introductions, not verified hotel-contract signatories. Do not rely on Sophie Fretwell as current buyer: CBHF’s contact page still lists her, but her professional employment history records a move to Brain Tumour Foundation of Canada in November 2026 and JA Canada advertised the CBHF/events manager role in October. Confirm the successor through Oli/Erin.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced 48th edition: Thursday, May 27, 2027, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Cocktail reception 17:00; dinner/program 18:00–21:00. These are activity times, not article dates. Within the requested horizon. No official 2028 date/venue announcement was located; annual recurrence must not be converted into a 2028 booking.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using supplied hotel capacities and the published gala format: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown is a plausible downtown lodging option for a limited out-of-town inductee, executive, sponsor or production cohort, not a replacement venue for the approximately 700-person gala. Its supplied 157-room inventory and approximately 224-banquet Admiral Ballroom cannot accommodate that dinner as one plenary banquet. The hotel’s own site places it near the MTCC/Entertainment District. Urban executive lodging fits better than a resort proposal. Any small meeting or reception is conditional on actual demand, space availability and confirmed catering capability; do not promise restaurant/lounge service. No defensible event-specific block size or overnight conversion is published.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 venue: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, North Building, Lower Level, 255 Front St. West, Toronto, Ontario. In Toronto proper, downtown/MTCC territory; not a hotel. Treat the main reception/dinner venue as committed for sales qualification, although the private contract was not inspected. No individual hall/room number is published on the event listing.
findings.historicalRotation: 2023-05-11 (44th), 2024-05-23 (45th), 2025-05-22 (46th), and 2026-05-28 (47th) all identify Metro Toronto Convention Centre, Toronto. The 2027 listing continues MTCC. This supports repeated Toronto/MTCC use, not destination rotation. Historical building/level details are not established by these sources; do not backfill the 2027 detail.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. Official 2027 event/participation pages publish no hotel names, host hotel, room block, booking code, housing bureau, accommodation RFP or overflow hotel. Every edition-specific listed hotel: none found in reviewed materials. Source text is about event participation, not housing: “Individual table and tickets are available for purchase” (Events); “Early bird sponsorship opportunities now available” (Participate). Neither quote establishes open lodging procurement. The October 2026 internal job description says the event manager will “Manage venue, production, décor, food & beverage, AV vendors and entertainment.” This identifies an internal event/vendor pathway but no hotel procurement mechanism. No published room-night or peak-room total found.
findings.organizationStructure: JA Canada is the national nonprofit youth-education organization and event owner/operator; CBHF is its signature fundraising event/brand property, not a separate PCO or commercial conference organizer. The October 2026 role description places CBHF/event execution inside JA Canada’s marketing/events team, reporting to the Director of Marketing within a team overseen by the Chief Development Officer. MTCC is the venue, not the organizer. No external PCO/DMC or housing agency was identified in reviewed edition materials.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The main 2027 reception/dinner is already publicly assigned to MTCC. No incumbent lodging hotel, hotel exclusivity, sold-out housing, displacement, or overflow demand was verified. MTCC proximity or a generic nearby-hotel listing is not a CBHF hotel commitment. The published 700/700+ annual audience is not 700 bedrooms; local attendance and overnight share are unknown.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Oli Maynard-Langedijk first, copying Erin Barton, with a short lodging-only introduction for May 27, 2027. Ask who currently leads CBHF event operations and who arranges accommodation for travelling inductees, sponsor executives and production staff. Ask whether any block/exclusivity exists, all contracted hotels, estimated out-of-town rooms, stay dates and decision timing. Offer a tailored proposal only after need and sourcing access are confirmed; do not lead with a 700-person gala or assume catering. If 2027 housing is committed, request permission to discuss the next Toronto cycle without inventing a 2028 date.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 gala venue capture is not an open opportunity on the evidence. Ancillary lodging accessibility is unconfirmed, not closed and not proven open. Ticket/table and sponsorship availability is not evidence of accommodation procurement. No organizer-approved booking or hotel RFP pathway has been published in reviewed materials.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeated MTCC use makes a future main-gala relocation pitch weak for this hotel’s capacity. Build a relationship for right-sized executive/sponsor lodging and genuinely requested side meetings associated with future Toronto editions. Annual recurrence is verified, but 2028 date, venue, hotel procurement timing and contestability are not announced in located official sources.
